result.question:
Build a verified census of every PUBLICLY DOWNLOADABLE dataset of real C-arm / mobile-fluoroscopy / cone-beam-CT-projection X-ray images of ANY anatomy (spine, pelvis, hip, knee, chest, head, phantoms, cadavers, animals), for the purpose of fitting a per-device image-formation model to each C-arm model. Paired data (raw or processed 2-D frames PLUS a CT of the same subject PLUS a known or recoverable projection pose/geometry) is the top priority because it allows a digitally reconstructed radiograph to be compared pixel-for-pixel with the real frame; unpaired real fluoroscopy is second priority; request-only / DUA-only sets go in a separate list.

ALREADY KNOWN (verify details, do not spend effort re-discovering; extend only): DeepFluoro (JHU, Siemens Cios Fusion, 6 cadaver pelves, 366 frames, poses; vendor DICOMs on JHU Dataverse), C-ArmLSpine (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22768651, FIRST/Yiying Surgio-B51, 149 lumbar cases, AP+LAT DR frames + CBCT), COBRA2026 (Elekta XVI kV CBCT projections, 145 pelvic RT patients with planning CT, four centres), Geneva hip gold-standard (D'Isidoro 2021, Philips BV Pulsera image intensifier, resin phantom, 19 poses), SpineSAC (five real C-arms, sawbone phantom, Google Drive), LUMOS, Veriserum (dual-plane knee phantom), CAMS-Knee, CM Spine (208 intraoperative lumbar G-arm, request), Pelphix (simulated + cadaver), LevelCheck (JHU, DUA), coronary angiography sets (CADICA, ARCADE, XCAD, AngioCAD), RTK example data, SPARK, RabbitCT, the Flepp femur fluoroscopy set (Zenodo 15753063 — verify), MIQR-CC (device metadata — verify), 2D-3D-GS.

QUESTIONS, each answered with a URL, license, download mechanism, and hard numbers (subjects, frames, image size, bit depth, raw vs processed, detector type, C-arm make/model, whether CT and pose are included):
1. Which additional public sets exist (2015–2026) with REAL C-arm or fluoroscopy frames: e.g. the LigaSure/ orthopaedic trauma sets, the Ljubljana / UL FE spine sets (Pernuš group: lumbar vertebra 2-D/3-D registration with C-arm images + CT — confirm public availability and device), the SpineWeb 2-D/3-D registration sets, the CBCT projection sets used for reconstruction benchmarks (Walnut CBCT is micro-CT — exclude industrial CT; include Elekta/Varian OBI/TrueBeam kV projection datasets with planning CT, e.g. the SPARE challenge, the 4D-CBCT AAPM sets, TCIA sets with kV projections), knee/hip fluoroscopy kinematics sets with CT models (e.g. from Stanford/Utah/Bern), dental/ENT C-arm sets, veterinary fluoroscopy, cardiac/vascular fluoroscopy with CT (e.g. the Coronary CTA + angiography paired sets), and endovascular device sets.
2. For every set: which C-arm MODEL produced it (Siemens Cios/Arcadis/Artis zeego, GE OEC 9900/Elite, Philips BV/Veradius/Zenition/Allura, Ziehm Vision/RFD, Medtronic O-arm, Brainlab Loop-X, Elekta XVI, Varian OBI/TrueBeam, Skanray, Fluorospot), the detector type (image intensifier vs flat panel, CsI vs GOS), pixel pitch and panel size, and whether frames are RAW detector signal or processed display images. If unknown, say unknown.
3. Which of these ship DICOM headers with vendor private tags (device settings kV/mA/pulse/filter/collimator) intact?
4. Datasets with CONSECUTIVE overlapping frames of one subject (sweeps, cine loops, kinematic sequences) at known displacement.
5. A count: how many DISTINCT C-arm models are represented across all public sets found (the k in "k devices").

Return a structured report: a table per priority tier with the fields above, exact citations (DOI/URL), and a final section listing what could not be verified. Flag anything where the download link is dead or the license forbids model training.
result.summary: Of the sources that survived verification, three deliver a genuinely paired real-frame + 3-D volume + recoverable pose package without a request step: the Geneva hip gold standard (Philips BV Pulsera image-intensifier C-arm, 19 frames, resin phantom, CT, calibrated projection matrix, CC BY-SA 4.0 on the repository), COBRA2026 (692 publicly downloadable pelvic-RT cases of the 867 total, from six centres on Elekta Synergy/VersaHD and Varian Halcyon/TrueBeam/VitalBeam linac-mounted kV CBCT, raw 16-bit projection sweeps of 189–895 frames with RTK geometry.xml and deformably registered planning CT, CC BY-NC 4.0), and the two Ljubljana sets (3D-2D-GS-CA: 10 cerebrovascular patients, 3D-DSA plus AP/LAT DSA frames with 4x4 detector pose and source position; 2D-3D-GS: cadaver L1–L5 with CT/MR and 18 turntable X-rays at 20° steps on a Trixell PIXIUM 4600 panel, not a C-arm; both CC BY-NC-ND). Veriserum (ETH custom bi-planar image-intensifier rig, ~110,990 knee-implant frames with per-frame poses, no CT, non-commercial) is a large unpaired-to-CT pose set; CAMS-Knee (modified BV Pulsera moving fluoroscope, six instrumented-TKR subjects) is request-only under a signed non-commercial licence. Three candidates contribute zero frames and must be struck from the census: the ETH tDPF paper (X-ray never switched on, share link 404), the Utah Hive Cam-FAIS record (CT, surfaces and transforms only), and the Calgary biplanar videoradiography paper (data declared unavailable). None of the verified sets ships DICOM with vendor private tags; COBRA2026 distils kV/mA/pulse/filter/collimator into metadata.yaml. The already-known COBRA2026 entry (145 patients, four centres, Elekta-only) is wrong on every count, and this batch adds no new named mobile C-arm model to k beyond the already-known Philips BV Pulsera; it adds at least two linac-mounted kV imaging platforms (Elekta, Varian) whose exact imager model names were not confirmed.

findings.claim: Geneva hip 2D-3D registration gold standard (D'Isidoro/Schmid 2021) is a TIER-1 paired set, downloadable anonymously with no request or DUA: Philips BV Pulsera video-fluoroscopy C-arm (image intensifier), 19 fluoroscopic frames of a resin female hip phantom at 1000x1000 px, 12-bit, 0.29 mm pixel, several kV settings, large rotations about the vertical axis; Philips Brilliance 64 CT (431x315x468, 0.78x0.78x1.0 mm, 140 kV); 21 3-mm fiducials; gold-standard rigid transforms CT->each view plus calibrated projection matrix (0.033 mm reprojection error); 481 files, 412.9 MB zip; formats TIFF/PNG/CSV/JSON (no DICOM, processed display frames, no vendor tags). Licence on the repository and DataCite is CC BY-SA 4.0 (no NC/ND), so model fitting is permitted with attribution and share-alike; the companion paper's text says CC BY-NC 4.0 for the dataset, a discrepancy to flag.
findings.evidence: Anonymous GET on access.yareta.unige.ch/access/metadata/<id> returned aip-access-level=PUBLIC, aip-dua=False, data-use-policy=LICENSE (CC BY-SA 4.0), 481 files / 413,203,728 bytes; a Range request on the download endpoint returned HTTP 206 with a zip signature and content-range 0-0/412867633, i.e. the full archive is served without login. DataCite rightsList: PUBLIC, BLUE, cc-by-sa-4.0. Paper Methods: 'A video-fluoroscopy C-arm (BV Pulsera, Philips Medical Systems) ... S = 19 2D images ... 1000 x 1000 square pixels and a grayscale dynamic range of 12 bits', 0.29 mm pixel, Brilliance CT 64 at 140 kV, 21 fiducials, ground-truth transforms from the MPPC method, rTRE 0.05 mm / uTRE 0.59 mm. Three verifiers unanimous on each of the three sub-claims (public, licence, tier-1 pairing). Not observed: the per-file listing (aip-content-structure-public=False) so shipped pose/calibration file names are inferred from the paper and the csv/json formats; rotation range is never quantified in degrees.

findings.claim: COBRA2026 (Thummerer, Rit, Kamp, Maspero et al.) is a TIER-1 paired CBCT-projection set that is far larger than the 'already known' entry: 867 pelvic radiotherapy patients from six European centres (UMC Utrecht, Medical University Vienna, Centre Leon Berard Lyon, LMU Munich, University Hospital Cologne, Medical University Graz; centres lettered A-D and F-G, E unused; per-centre 150/134/150/150/116/167), split 692 train / 52 validation / 123 test, ~950 GB. Centres A-D are Elekta linac-mounted kV CBCT on Synergy/VersaHD (504x504 px, 0.8x0.8 mm, 120 kV, 189-734 projections/scan); F-G are Varian on Halcyon/TrueBeam/VitalBeam (1024-3072 x 384-768 px, 0.28-0.39 x 0.39-1.12 mm, 125-140 kV, 406-895 projections/scan). Only the 692-case training split (~750 GB) is downloadable today; validation and test are embargoed until 2032-03-01. Licence CC BY-NC 4.0 (training permitted, commercial use forbidden). The 'already known' figures (145 patients, four centres, Elekta-only) appear in no primary source. These are linac-mounted kV imagers, not mobile C-arms.
findings.evidence: Zenodo API: version 1.0.0, licence cc-by-nc-4.0, description names six centres and sizes Train ~750 GB / Val ~60 GB / Test ~140 GB. arXiv 2607.20037 Table 4: A 150, B 134, C 150, D 150, F 116, G 167 = 867; train 692, val 52, test 123. Table 1: Manufacturer Elekta x4 / Varian x2; Linac Synergy, VersaHD | Synergy, VersaHD | Synergy | Synergy, VersaHD | Halcyon, TrueBeam | TrueBeam, VitalBeam; 120 kV vs 125-140 kV. Paper: 'The validation and test sets will remain under embargo until March 2032'. Independent check: Girder COBRA2026_Train folder (public=true) holds A=120, B=107, C=120, D=120, F=92, G=133 case folders = 692; COBRA2026_Val folder is empty; anonymous HEAD on an item download returned HTTP 200 with no login. The strings '145', 'four cent', 'XVI', 'OBI' and 'flat panel' occur zero times in the paper, so the exact kV-imager model names (XVI generation, OBI/TrueBeam imager version) are not stated; a claim assigning 'at least four distinct imaging-system models' to COBRA2026 was refuted 0-3.

findings.claim: Every downloadable COBRA2026 case is a complete real-frame / CT / pose package for DRR-vs-frame comparison, and every scan is a consecutive gantry sweep at known per-frame angle: projections.mha (measured detector signal, 16-bit unsigned, stacked without conversion to line integrals; Elekta frames already flood-field corrected by the vendor on export; Varian .xim stacked likewise), geometry.xml (RTK ThreeDCircularGeometry with per-projection GantryAngle, ProjectionOffsetX/Y and 3x4 matrix, SID 1000 / SDD 1536 verified on case A002 with 356 projections), ct_original.mha, ct_def.mha and ct_def_masked.mha (planning CT rigidly then B-spline deformably registered in Elastix to the daily CBCT anatomy, origins shifted to the CBCT isocenter), cbct_clinical.mha, cbct_rtk.mha, FOV masks, projections_simulated.mha (forward projection of ct_def with the same geometry plus simulated scatter, Poisson noise and a randomized respiratory-motion model), metadata.yaml and reconstruction.yaml (Elekta) or Scan.xml + Calibrations/ (Varian). metadata.yaml carries device settings (A002: Elekta, 120 kV, 80 mA, 40 ms pulse, KVFilter F1, Collimator M20, half fan, 504x504 @ 0.8 mm, 356 frames; planning CT Philips Big Bore 0.74 mm / 3 mm). Frames per sweep 189-895 overall. No DICOM headers ship; vendor .his/.xim are converted to MetaImage.
sources: https://tomoradio-warehouse.creatis.insa-lyon.fr/api/v1 (case A002 geometry.xml and metadata.yaml downloaded; case F003 listed)
findings.evidence: Zenodo description: 'Each case directory ... contains: projections.mha Measured raw CBCT projection images, geometry.xml Cone-beam acquisition geometry in RTK format, projections_simulated.mha ... ct_original.mha, ct_def.mha, ct_def_masked.mha, cbct_clinical.mha, cbct_rtk.mha ...'. Paper: 'The acquisition geometry was extracted from Frames.xml, converted into an RTK geometry object using the RTK Elekta geometry reader' (Varian: Scan.xml + .xim headers via the RTK Varian reader); 'measured X-ray detector signal stored as 16-bit unsigned integers'; 'For Elekta acquisitions, the exported projection images had already undergone flood-field correction prior to export'; 'The spatial origins of all released volumetric images were subsequently shifted such that they align with the CBCT acquisition isocenter'. Verifier downloaded A002/geometry.xml anonymously (HTTP 200): <RTKThreeDCircularGeometry version=3>, SourceToIsocenterDistance 1000, SourceToDetectorDistance 1536, 356 Projection blocks with GantryAngle (first three 180.0244, 180.0257, 180.0263 deg - gantry ramp-up, so increments are recorded, not uniform), ProjectionOffsetX -112.13 (half-fan panel shift). A002 and F003 each hold all 13 files (projections.mha 110 MB / 656 MB; projections_simulated.mha 181 MB / 960 MB). Authors' own qualification: ct_def 'do not represent exact ground-truth representations of the CBCT anatomy; residual local misalignments remain ... particularly apparent at the body contour', so the pairing is deformable, not a rigid patient pose. A finer-grained claim about scatter grids, offset-detector counts and Varian air-scan normalisation of the released projections was refuted 0-3, so treat those details as unverified.

findings.claim: Veriserum (ETH Zurich Laboratory for Movement Biomechanics; DOI 10.3929/ethz-b-000701146; MICCAI 2025, arXiv 2509.05483) is a large dual-plane pose-annotated fluoroscopy set but NOT CT-paired and NOT a commercial C-arm: a custom bi-planar rig of two X-ray tubes, two collimators and two analogue image intensifiers coupled to high-speed cameras, planes at 110 +/- 0.5 deg, source-intensifier distances 1850 and 1855 mm, 360 mm intensifiers, 40 kV / 25 mA, 1664 x 1600 px frames captured at 25 or 30 Hz. ~110,990 images of 10 knee-implant pair combinations (2 femur x 5 tibia, aluminium phantoms from Zimmer Biomet CAD models) over 1,600 robot-driven trials (HORST600 six-axis robot, +/-0.05 mm), every image with an automatically registered pose and 200 (paper) / 390 (README SQLite DB) manually registered poses; distortion-corrected images plus raw calibration-grid images. No manufacturer of tube, intensifier or camera is named anywhere. Data rights on ETH Research Collection are 'In Copyright - Non-Commercial Use Permitted' (the CC BY 4.0 belongs to the paper). Bit depth and raw-vs-processed status are not stated.
sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05483 (Wang, Vogl, Schutz, Cukovic, Taylor, MICCAI 2025)
findings.evidence: Paper Sec. 2.1 verbatim: 'two X-ray tubes, two collimators, and two X-ray image intensifiers connected to high-speed cameras, all constructed in a bi-planar configuration ... mounted at an angle of 110 +/- 0.5 deg, with source-intensifier distances of 1850 and 1855 mm, and intensifier sizes of 360 mm ... tube voltage of 40 kV and a tube current of 25 mA ... 1664 x 1600 pixels'; limitations: 'captured using analogue source-intensifier technology rather than digital flat panels'. Abstract: 'approximately 110,000 X-ray images of 10 knee implant pair combinations (2 femur and 5 tibia implants) captured during 1,600 trials ... Each image is annotated with an automatically registered ground-truth pose, while 200 images include manually registered poses'; full text gives 110,990. Grep of the paper for Siemens/Philips/GE/OEC/Ziehm/Shimadzu/Toshiba/Canon/Varex/Thales/Photron/Basler/PCO/Cios/Pulsera/'C-arm' returned zero hits. Caveat: the ETH landing page returned HTTP 500 on two attempts during verification, so live download availability was not confirmed at that moment; treat as a transient error and re-check.

findings.claim: CAMS-Knee (ETH Zurich + Julius Wolff Institute/Charite; Taylor et al., J Biomech 2017, DOI 10.1016/j.jbiomech.2017.09.022) belongs in the REQUEST-ONLY / DUA tier: real single-plane moving-fluoroscope sequences (a modified Philips BV Pulsera C-arm, image intensifier read by a CCD camera, 1000x1000 px, 12-bit, pulsed 25 Hz / 8 ms, ~60-70 kV, 10-12 mA, servo-tracked) of six subjects with instrumented total knee replacements during level walking, stair descent and ramp descent, registered per frame to implant CAD models (not to a subject CT). The full set, including 'Fluoroscopic Images' as a selectable data type, is released only after an online form plus an uploaded signed institutional licence (non-exclusive, non-sub-licensable, project-only, no commercial use, no third parties, data destruction on project completion, mandatory citation), delivered by a personalized time-limited link. The only licence-free item is a single-subject level-walking + squat sample behind a click-through registration form, containing processed registered overlays (fluoro_reg_img), not raw frames.
findings.evidence: ETH page: 'TKR kinematics (moving fluoroscope, 3D reconstruction of tibio-femoral implant kinematics) ... normal walking, stair descent and ramp descent'; 'An example trial of level walking from a single subject can be downloaded without license agreement'. Data Request page: 'Upload Signed License Agreement - (pdf required)'; 'you will receive a personalized time-limited download link'; T&C verbatim: 'The data may only be used for scientific purposes without any commercial benefit. The data is only intendend for use at the registered institute or facility and may not be passed on to third parties.' Licence PDF (HTTP 200, 183,616 B) Sec. 3: 'not use the CAMS-Knee Data for commercial purposes or profit', 'not sub-license, make available, market, sell ... to any third party'. List 2017 PLoS ONE describes the device as a modified BV Pulsera (Philips) with 1000x1000 12-bit II/CCD imaging at 25 Hz. Sample description PDF v1.1 (2023-02-08): one subject (K8L), gait + squat, 'fluoro_reg_img' folder of fluoroscopic captured images/video including the 3D implant components. One verifier dissented on the licence claim only because the quoted sentence sits on the orthoload request page, not the cited ETH page; the substance was confirmed by all three. Not verified: nominal pixel pitch in mm and whether the full-set frames are raw detector output or processed exports.

findings.claim: Ljubljana 3D-2D-GS-CA (Mitrovic and Spiclin, LIT FE UL; TMI 2013 DOI 10.1109/TMI.2013.2259844) is a directly downloadable TIER-1-style paired set with recoverable geometry but with a 3D-DSA rotational volume rather than a CT, processed frames, and an unnamed C-arm: 10 cerebrovascular patients (8 aneurysm, 2 AVM), each with one 3D-DSA (512x512x391, 0.4646 mm isotropic, int16) and four 2-D images (2D-DSA and 2D-MAX at AP and LAT, i.e. two distinct poses), each 2480x1920 px at 0.154 mm pitch stored as float32 intensities normalised to 0-1 in an in-house .rad/.raw format carrying a 4x4 detector pose (TPosition) and SourcePosition in world coordinates; source-to-detector distance ~1196 mm (AP) and ~1250 mm (LAT); fiducial-derived gold standard with mTRE 0.033-0.077 mm (user guide; per-case xls max 0.0565). Ten zips of 85-120 MB plus a 1 MB gold-standard zip, HTTP 200, Last-Modified 2013-05-07, no login or form; page licence CC BY-NC-ND, but the bundled 2013 user guide says use requires a signed agreement with the lab. No DICOM, no vendor tags, no cine or sweep sequences. It is not the later 15-patient (Med Phys 2015) or 25-patient (IJCARS 2018) database, neither of which is downloadable.
findings.evidence: Page: 'A database of 3D-DSA, 2D-DSA and 2D-MAX images for 10 patients with two cerebrovascular pathologies and corresponding gold standard registrations obtained by aligning fiducial markers ... License Creative Commons (CC): BY-NC-ND'. curl -I on all ten zips: HTTP 200, Content-Length 89,029,734-125,516,920 B, Last-Modified 2013-05-07; gold-standard zip 1,015,177 B. Verifier unpacked dataset01 and dataset02: Dataset1_2D_{DSA,MAX}_{AP,LAT}.rad/.raw each 'Size[pixels] 2480 1920, Step[mm] 0.154 0.154, DataType float', raw = 19,046,400 B = 2480*1920*4, min 0 / max 1; TPosition det(R)=1.0000; SDD computed 1196.4 mm (AP) and 1249.5 mm (LAT); 3D-DSA MET_SHORT 512x512x391 @ 0.464564 mm. Guide Sec. 3.2: 'the numbers after the TPosition: desrcibe the rigid transformation matrix Ts which relates the 2D image coordinate system Ss to world coordinate system Sw and xs, ys, zs are coordinates of the X-ray source'; 'The raw file is comprised of Nx*Ny float values representing the 2D image intensities between 0 and 1'. Guide p.2: 'This gold standard data can only be obtained and used after signing the agreement form' - not enforced by the server. C-arm model: not stated anywhere verified; 2480x1920 at 0.154 mm = 38.2 x 29.6 cm panel is consistent with a Siemens Artis 30x40 flat panel but that is inference only. One verifier dissented on the geometry claim over the wording 'single AP and LAT frames' (there are four images at two poses) and the identity 3D-DSA pose; the measured numbers were confirmed by all three.

findings.claim: Ljubljana 2D-3D-GS lumbar spine gold standard (Tomazevic, Likar, Pernus, MICCAI 2002) is public and CT-paired with an 18-frame known-displacement rotational sequence, but was NOT acquired with a C-arm and contributes no C-arm model to k: cadaver L1-L5 of an 80-year-old female; GE HiSpeed CT/i at 100 kV (0.273x0.273x1 mm) and Philips Gyroscan NT Intera 1.5 T MR (0.39x0.39x1.9 mm); 18 X-ray images at 20.000 deg turntable steps (source and detector fixed, phantom rotated), 1560x1560 px at 0.286 mm, float, each with a 4x4 detector pose and source position, source-to-detector-plane 1009.6 mm on every frame; detector Trixell PIXIUM 4600 flat panel (429x429 mm, 0.143 mm pixels, 14-bit), images 3x3 median-filtered and 2x subsampled; gold-standard TRE ~0.15-0.26 mm (CT) and ~0.24-0.42 mm (MR). Single 79,049,365-byte zip, HTTP 200, Last-Modified 2021-06-16, direct link, CC BY-NC-ND (the 2003 guide's 'on request after signing the agreement' is superseded by the 2021 web release). No DICOM.
sources: Tomazevic, Likar, Pernus, 'Gold Standard 2D/3D Registration of X-ray to CT and MR Images', MICCAI 2002 (Documents/Miccai2002_paper.pdf inside the zip)
findings.evidence: MICCAI 2002 paper verbatim: 'X-ray images were captured by PIXIUM 4600 (Trixell) digital X-ray detector. The detector had a 429x429 mm active surface, with 0.143x0.143 mm pixel size and 14-bit dynamic range. To simulate C-arm acquisition X-ray source and sensor plane were fixed while the spine phantom was rotated on a turntable ... By rotating (step=20 deg) the spine phantom around its long axis, 18 X-ray images were acquired'; 'filtered by 3x3 median filter and then sub-sampled by the factor of two' (0.143 x 2 = 0.286 mm matches headers). Verifier read every im000-im017.rad header (Size 1560 1560, Step 0.286, DataType float, TPosition, SourcePosition), computed SDD 1009.6 mm on all 18 frames and successive rotation 20.000 deg (range 19.9999-20.0001) on all 17 steps; CT .sta 'Step[mm]: 0.273438 0.273438 1', MR .sta 0.390625 0.390625 1.9. curl -I: HTTP 200, application/zip, Content-Length 79049365, Last-Modified Wed, 16 Jun 2021. Two minor defects noted: the claim's cited URL was the sibling CA page (misattribution; the text is verbatim from the bundled paper), and 1560 px x 0.286 mm = 446 mm exceeds the stated 429 mm active area - an inconsistency in the original description.

findings.claim: Three candidate sources contribute ZERO downloadable fluoroscopy frames and must be excluded from both the paired and unpaired tiers: (a) the ETH Zurich tracking dual-plane fluoroscope (tDPF) paper (Planta et al., PLoS One 2025-07-24, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0328351) - the X-ray subsystems (two Thales TH 9447 QX H694 L VR70 intensifiers, two Varian G1082 tubes, two Phantom VEO E-340L cameras) were never switched on, only motion-capture data were collected, and its polybox share (YOL7U9zVFU0MIdO) returns a genuine HTTP 404 on both the share and /download; (b) the Utah Hive Cam-FAIS dual-fluoroscopy record (DOI 10.7278/S5d-btv7-ztpw, CC BY 3.0, 2025-09-30) - the 3.16 GB zip holds only hip and knee CT (.nii.gz), CT-derived femur/pelvis surfaces (.k), landmarks, demographics, event-frame indices and per-timepoint bone-to-lab rigid transforms (.txt, two 1x16 matrices) for Cam_03-09 and Norm_02-15; no image, video, calibration or source/detector geometry file is listed, so bone poses exist but cannot be rendered; (c) the University of Calgary high-speed biplanar videoradiography knee paper (Zhang, Lichti, Kuntze, Ronsky, Diagnostics 2024;14:1488, DOI 10.3390/diagnostics14141488) - Data Availability Statement 'The data are unavailable due to privacy restrictions' (MDPI's unavailable template, not the on-request template), no supplementary or repository link, no dataset found on Zenodo, Dryad or Calgary Scholaris; the rig is custom (Varian G-1086 tubes, Toshiba E5876SD-P2A 406 mm intensifiers, PCO DIMAX cameras, 2016x2016 px, 12-20 Hz) and the in vivo bone models were MRI-derived, so it could never have been CT-paired.

Utah record description: 'a collection of: a. hip 3D clinical computed tomography (CT) images (.nii) b. surface files ... (.k) c. activity/ rigid body transforms/ kinematic transform activities (.txt)'; files API lists exactly two files (README 21,236 B; Hive_Cam_FAIS_Biomechanics.zip 3,159,520,263 B); README enumerates Participant_Demographics.xlsx, Event_Frames.xlsx, SubjID_{Femur,Femur_Pelvis,Pelvis,Knee}.k, SubjID_Landmarks.xlsx, SubjID_Hip_CT.nii.gz, SubjID_Knee_CT.nii.gz, DFS_SubjID_[Activity].txt; a targeted search of the README for image/TIFF/DICOM/video/frame/calibration/geometry/camera/detector/pixel/distortion found only methods prose; 3.16 GB is far too small for 100 Hz dual-view fluoroscopy across eight activities. Calgary: PMC full text carries 'The data are unavailable due to privacy restrictions'; the word 'C-arm' does not occur; Dryad API count 0, Zenodo and Scholaris searches returned no release. Caveats: the Utah zip was not opened (verdict rests on the README enumeration); a separate claim detailing the Utah device (Radiological Imaging Services, 100 Hz, 78-100 kVp) was refuted 0-3, so the device specification for that rig should be treated as unverified even though the README prose was quoted.

findings.claim: Cross-cutting answers to questions 3-5 from the verified material. (Q3, DICOM with vendor private tags) NONE of the verified sets ships DICOM: Geneva is TIFF/PNG/CSV/JSON; both Ljubljana sets are in-house .rad/.raw float; Veriserum's format is not stated as DICOM; COBRA2026 converts Elekta .his and Varian .xim into MetaImage and distils device settings (manufacturer, kV, mA, pulse length, kV filter, collimator, fan mode, imager size, frame count) into metadata.yaml, with the Elekta .INI reconstruction file and Varian Scan.xml + Calibrations/ folders retained - the richest device-settings record in the batch, but not DICOM. (Q4, consecutive frames at known displacement) COBRA2026: every case is one continuous gantry sweep of 189-895 overlapping frames with a recorded angle per frame (692 public sweeps); Ljubljana 2D-3D-GS: 18 frames at exactly 20.000 deg turntable steps (not a C-arm); Veriserum: 1,600 robot-driven trials captured at 25-30 Hz with a pose on every frame (no CT); CAMS-Knee: 25 Hz gait/stair/ramp sequences (request-only). Geneva (19 discrete orientations) and 3D-2D-GS-CA (two single views) are not sweeps. (Q5, k) This batch confirms only ONE named commercial C-arm model with public frames, the Philips BV Pulsera (Geneva; and, in modified form, the request-only CAMS-Knee) - already on the known list, so no increment to k from mobile C-arms. It adds two linac-mounted kV vendor platforms (Elekta on Synergy/VersaHD; Varian on Halcyon/TrueBeam/VitalBeam) whose imager model names (XVI generation, OBI/TrueBeam imager version) the paper never states - a claim that COBRA2026 contributes 'at least four distinct imaging-system models' was refuted 0-3, so count it as 2 vendor families with model resolution pending. The Ljubljana CA C-arm is unknown (likely a Siemens Artis-class 30x40 flat panel by pixel geometry, unconfirmed). Veriserum, the Utah rig and the Calgary rig are custom image-intensifier assemblies, not nameable C-arm models. Licence flags for model training: COBRA2026 CC BY-NC (non-commercial); both Ljubljana sets CC BY-NC-ND (no derivatives, non-commercial, and a signed-agreement clause in the old guides); Veriserum non-commercial; CAMS-Knee non-commercial + no redistribution; Geneva CC BY-SA on the repository but CC BY-NC in the paper text. Dead link: the tDPF polybox share (404); ETH Research Collection landing page for Veriserum returned HTTP 500 during checking (likely transient).
findings.evidence: Synthesised from the per-dataset verifier evidence above: COBRA2026 A002/metadata.yaml fields (Manufacturer Elekta, TubeVoltage 120, TubeCurrent 80, PulseLength 40, KVFilter F1, Collimator M20, Fan Half, ImagerSize 504x504 @ 0.8 mm, Frames 356) and paper Table 3 (reconstruction.yaml from Elekta .INI; Scan.xml + Calibrations/ for Varian); Geneva formats list from the Yareta OAI-PMH record (image/tiff, image/png, text/csv, application/json ... no DICOM); Ljubljana zips contain only .rad/.raw/.mhd/.sta/.txt; the COBRA2026 paper uses neither 'XVI' nor 'OBI' nor 'flat panel'; Veriserum paper names no manufacturer; the 'k >= 4 from COBRA2026' claim and two detailed COBRA raw-vs-corrected claims are in the refuted list (0-3 each).
findings.vote: synthesis of 3-0 and 2-1 claims; contradicting device-model claim refuted 0-3

result.caveats: Scope: this synthesis covers only the 19 claims that survived verification in this round; it does not re-verify the 'already known' list (DeepFluoro, C-ArmLSpine, SpineSAC, LUMOS, Pelphix, LevelCheck, coronary sets, RTK, RabbitCT, Flepp femur, MIQR-CC) and does not report on the LigaSure/orthopaedic-trauma, SpineWeb, TCIA kV-projection, 4D-CBCT AAPM, dental/ENT, veterinary, or endovascular searches asked for in Question 1 - no confirmed claim addressed them, so they remain uncovered rather than absent. SPARE (hdl.handle.net/2123/34378) had every claim refuted 0-3 (real Varian half-fan / Elekta full-fan composition, simulated-set patient count), so its contents, vendors and real/simulated split are unverified and it should be listed under 'could not be verified', not in a tier. Licence discrepancies are real and unresolved: Geneva repository/DataCite say CC BY-SA 4.0 while the Med Phys paper says CC BY-NC 4.0 for the dataset; both Ljubljana pages say CC BY-NC-ND while the bundled 2003/2013 guides demand a signed agreement (not enforced by the server); Veriserum data are 'In Copyright - Non-Commercial Use Permitted' on ETH Research Collection although the paper is CC BY 4.0. Several verifiers exhausted their WebSearch budget (200/200) and fell back to direct fetches and repository APIs, so third-party contradiction searches were incomplete for Veriserum, CAMS-Knee, Ljubljana CA and Calgary. Not directly observed: the Geneva per-file listing (whole-archive download only; pose/calibration file names inferred from the paper), the Utah 3.2 GB zip contents (verdict rests on the README), and COBRA2026 validation/test cases (empty on Girder, embargoed to 2032-03-01). Time-sensitive: the Veriserum landing page returned HTTP 500 twice on 2026-09-22 and should be re-checked; COBRA2026 counts (692 public of 867) are as of the July 2026 release; the Yareta archive retention runs to 2031-03-10. Device-model resolution for COBRA2026 is the weakest point: the paper identifies imaging only by linac (Synergy/VersaHD; Halcyon/TrueBeam/VitalBeam) and the claim that this yields four-plus distinct imaging-system models was refuted, so the k contribution is stated as two vendor families, not a model count. The 2-1 votes (CAMS-Knee licence, Ljubljana CA geometry) were dissents over citation placement and wording, not over the facts.
openQuestions: Which C-arm produced the Ljubljana 3D-2D-GS-CA angiography frames? The 2480x1920 px / 0.154 mm geometry (38.2 x 29.6 cm panel) suggests a Siemens Artis-class 30x40 flat panel, but the TMI 2013 paper text was not checked and nothing in the package names the device.

What are the exact kV-imager models behind COBRA2026's six centres (XVI hardware/software generation on Synergy vs VersaHD; OBI/TrueBeam imager version on Halcyon vs TrueBeam vs VitalBeam), and do the per-centre metadata.yaml or reconstruction.yaml files record enough (panel model, software version) to distinguish them for a per-device formation model? The paper never uses 'XVI', 'OBI' or 'flat panel'.

Does the Geneva Yareta archive actually ship the 19 gold-standard rigid transforms and the calibrated projection matrix as files (the csv/json formats and the paper imply it), and what bit depth and processing state are the TIFF/PNG frames in? Only the whole-archive zip is served, so this needs a download and inspection.

What is SPARE's true composition (real Varian/Elekta clinical kV projections vs Monte-Carlo simulated sets, patient counts, vendor models) - every claim about it was refuted, so it needs a fresh pass from Instructions_Datasets.doc inside the archive rather than from the landing page.

For Veriserum: are the ~110,990 frames raw camera output or distortion-corrected/display-processed, at what bit depth, and is the ETH Research Collection record downloadable today (HTTP 500 during checking)? Also, does the README's 390 manually matched poses supersede the paper's 200?

refuted.claim: The kV imaging systems are linac-mounted CBCT, not mobile C-arms: centres A–D used Elekta XVI on Synergy and VersaHD linacs; centres F and G used Varian OBI on Halcyon, TrueBeam and VitalBeam. For the k-devices count this contributes at least four distinct imaging-system models (Elekta Synergy, Elekta VersaHD, Varian TrueBeam, Varian Halcyon; plus VitalBeam), all flat-panel.

Projections are raw (not log/line-integral converted) 16-bit unsigned detector frames. Elekta: 504×504 px at 0.8×0.8 mm, 120 kV, 20–80 mA, 32–40 ms pulses, 189–499 projections per scan, no scatter grid, mostly full 360° arcs with offset detector (centre A: offset 129 / centred 21; full 142 / half 8). Varian: 1024–3072 × 384–768 px at 0.28–0.39 × 0.39–1.12 mm, 125–140 kV, 30–90 mA, 14.3–20 ms, 406–895 projections, scatter grid present. Vendor formats (Elekta .his, Varian .xim) were converted to compressed MetaImage; vendor headers are NOT shipped intact but distilled into metadata.yaml / reconstruction.yaml, so DICOM private tags are not available.

The released projections are measured detector signal (16-bit unsigned, 0–65535), not line integrals; however Elekta frames were already flood-field corrected by the vendor before export, and Varian frames are normalised against an air scan at the nearest gantry angle with a kernel-based scatter correction applied — so they are corrected detector signal, not raw uncorrected panel readout.

The public SPARE archive contains REAL clinical kV CBCT projection data from two vendors, each paired with a prior 4D-CT of the same patient: a Varian half-fan set (5 patients, 30 scans) and an Elekta full-fan set (6 patients, 24 scans). The authors' page names only the vendor ('a Varian system', 'an Elekta system'); the specific model (OBI/TrueBeam, XVI/Synergy), detector, pixel pitch and raw-vs-processed status are NOT stated anywhere in the landing page, README or challenge page. Clinical data were contributed by UT Southwestern (Xun Jia group).

The largest component of SPARE is NOT real detector data: it is Monte-Carlo simulated CBCT projections (primary + scatter + quantum noise) generated from 4D-Lung CT volumes, 32 scans, in three variants (no scatter, scatter, low dose). The patient count is inconsistent between sources — the Med Phys abstract says nine patients, the challenge page says 12 patients — so the simulated-set headcount must be checked against Instructions_Datasets.doc inside the archive.

The imaging device is a custom biplane image-intensifier rig, not a commercial C-arm: two X-ray emitter / image-intensifier pairs on independent bases built by Radiological Imaging Services (Hamburg, PA), run at 100 Hz, 78-100 kVp, 1.9-3.2 mAs, 4.5-7.0 ms camera exposure. Intensifier diameter, camera model, pixel matrix and bit depth are not stated in the record or the paper. For the 'k devices' count this is a distinct custom II system, not a Siemens/GE/Philips/Ziehm C-arm model.
